message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Year | Key Parties | Main Issue |
|---|--------|------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | Mutual excommunication over theological, liturgical, and political differences (e.g., papal primacy, the Filioque clause). |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 | Various European reformers (e.g., Martin Luther, John Calvin) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Reformers challenged Catholic doctrines and practices (e.g., indulgences, authority of Scripture vs. tradition). |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of 1965** | 1965 | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | A formal declaration of the mutual excommunication that had been in place since 1054, reaffirming the split and clarifying the status of the two churches. |

These three events represent the most profound and lasting divisions within Christianity, each reshaping the religious, cultural, and political landscape of their time.
